Sensors._comment_imu: BMI088-class noise model (the unit on the real IFS-08). Datasheet noise densities: accel 175 µg/√Hz, gyro 0.014 °/s/√Hz. At 400 Hz sample rate (200 Hz Nyquist BW) those become ~0.024 m/s² and ~0.0035 rad/s per-sample standard deviations. Bias drift is modelled as Ornstein–Uhlenbeck with a 100 s correlation time, a typical bench-test characteristic for a MEMS IMU at FS race-car operating temperatures.

Lidar1._comment_lidar: Hesai ATX_S01 datasheet (Section 1.4): 1-D rotating mirror (hybrid solid-state), 116 ch, 120° H × 18.3° V FoV (-12.4° to +5.9°), 10 Hz, ~1.74 M pts/s @ 0.08° H, 3 cm 1σ range. PointsPerSecond is set to 1.0 M (not the datasheet 1.74 M) deliberately for the sim. The real car runs the sensor on dedicated hardware with no rendering / physics / SLAM-pipeline competition; in PIE the LiDAR scan competes for CPU with everything else (Cone_Detection alone scaled linearly with point count and was hitting 4 cores at 1.74 M). 1.0 M keeps the sensor saturating its 10 Hz publish rate while leaving headroom for the rest of the autonomy stack. Bumping back to 1.74 M is a one-line change here when running benchmarks vs the real-car captures. Wire rate is the hit-rate fraction of attempted rays (~65 % in an outdoor scene); at 1.0 M attempted that lands ~650 k pts/s of valid returns at /lidar/Lidar1.
Lidar1._comment_mount: Mount aligned with the IFS-08's actual LiDAR position: X=0 (CoG-aligned, just beneath the main hoop), Y=0 (centered), Z=1.10 m (main hoop crossbar height). Previously X=0.5 m / Z=0.9 m was a hood-mount approximation; correcting it shifts the sensor back ~50 cm and up ~20 cm, which changes both the cone-detection range envelope (cones at the rear become visible) and the time-to-first-detection for cones immediately ahead. Verify cone_detection still classifies cluster heights correctly after re-baselining.
